1.q: וַ⁠תִּקְרַ֜בְנָה בְּנ֣וֹת צְלָפְחָ֗ד בֶּן חֵ֤פֶר בֶּן גִּלְעָד֙ בֶּן מָכִ֣יר בֶּן מְנַשֶּׁ֔ה לְ⁠מִשְׁפְּחֹ֖ת מְנַשֶּׁ֣ה בֶן יוֹסֵ֑ף
1.note: Here the author is introducing **the daughters of Zelophehad** as new participants in the story. Your language may have its own way of introducing new participants that you can use in your translation. Alternate translation: [Now there was a man named Zelophehad, the son of Hepher, the son of Gilead, the son of Machir, the son of Manasseh, of the clans of Manasseh the son of Joseph, and his daughters came near]

2.q: לִ⁠פְנֵ֣י מֹשֶׁ֗ה וְ⁠לִ⁠פְנֵי֙ אֶלְעָזָ֣ר הַ⁠כֹּהֵ֔ן וְ⁠לִ⁠פְנֵ֥י הַ⁠נְּשִׂיאִ֖ם
2.note: Here, **the face of** represents the presence of a person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before Moses and before Eleazar the priest and before the leaders]

3.note: The pronoun **he** refers to Zelophehad, the father of these women. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [and Zelophehad was not in the midst of the congregation]

The implication is that Zelophehad had no sons who could receive his property. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [and he had no sons to inherit his property]

4.q: לָ֣⁠מָּה יִגָּרַ֤ע שֵׁם אָבִ֨י⁠נוּ֙ מִ⁠תּ֣וֹךְ מִשְׁפַּחְתּ֔⁠וֹ כִּ֛י אֵ֥ין ל֖⁠וֹ בֵּ֑ן
4.note: The daughters of Zelophehad are using the question form to insist that it would be wrong for their father to be forgotten among his relatives just because he had no son. If a speaker of your language would not use the question form for that purpose, you could translate this as a statement or as an exclamation. Alternate translation: [The name of our father should not be taken away from the midst of his clan just because there is not for him a son!]

4.q: לָ֣⁠מָּה יִגָּרַ֤ע שֵׁם אָבִ֨י⁠נוּ֙ מִ⁠תּ֣וֹךְ מִשְׁפַּחְתּ֔⁠וֹ
4.note: The expression **be taken away** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Why should the name of our father disappear from the midst of his clan]

Here, **the name of our father** represents the memory of him and his continuing place among his relatives. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [should the memory of our father be lost from the midst of his clan]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **a possession**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [Give to us land that we may own]

5.note: If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **judgment**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [And Moses presented what they were requesting to be decided]
Here, **the face of** represents the presence of Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before Yahweh]

7.note: If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **a possession** and **an inheritance**, you could express the same ideas in another way. Alternate translation: [land that they will own and that their descendants will inherit]

Yahweh is using the possessive form to describe a **possession** that is characterized by **an inheritance**. If a speaker of your language would not use the possessive form for this, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [an inherited possession]

8.q: אִ֣ישׁ כִּֽי יָמ֗וּת וּ⁠בֵן֙ אֵ֣ין ל֔⁠וֹ
8.note: The implication is that the man has no son who could receive his property. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [A man, when he dies and there is no son to receive his property]

8.q: אִ֣ישׁ כִּֽי יָמ֗וּת וּ⁠בֵן֙ אֵ֣ין ל֔⁠וֹ
8.note: Yahweh is not referring to a specific **man**. He means men in general. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Suppose a man dies and there is not a son for him]
If it would be more natural in your language, you may want to put the information about **A man** with the information about when **he dies**. Alternate translation: [When a man dies]

11.note: Here, **his flesh** represents the closest blood relative of a person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [to his blood relative]

The pronoun **it** refers to the instructions about inheritance that Yahweh has just given. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And these instructions shall be for the sons of Israel for a statute of judgment]
If your language does not use abstract nouns for the ideas of **a statute** and **judgment**, you could express the same ideas in another way. Alternate translation: [for deciding cases legally]

Yahweh is speaking of himself in the third person as **Yahweh**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could translate this in the first person. Alternate translation: [just as I, Yahweh, have commanded Moses]

13.note: The expression **be gathered** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [and go to be with your peoples]

Yahweh is referring to the death of Moses in a polite way by using the phrase **be gathered to your peoples**. Depending on what is helpful for your readers, you could use a polite way of referring to this in your language, or you could state this plainly. Alternate translation: [and then die]

Here Yahweh is using the plural **peoples** where he could have used the singular form. This suggests that he is using the plural form to refer to all of the relatives and ancestors of Moses who had already died. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use the singular and express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [your people who died before you]

The expression **was gathered** is a passive verbal form. If it would be unnatural to use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [just as I gathered Aaron your brother]

14.note: Here, **my mouth** represents what Yahweh had commanded. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [you rebelled against my command]
If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **strife**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [when the congregation quarreled]

The implication is that Moses and Aaron were to honor Yahweh as holy while the people were watching. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [to honor me as holy]

Here, **their eyes** represents the watching presence of the people. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in their sight]

14.q: הֵ֛ם מֵֽי מְרִיבַ֥ת קָדֵ֖שׁ מִדְבַּר צִֽן
14.note: Here the author is providing background information to help readers understand what happens next in the story. In your translation, introduce this information in a way that would be natural in your own language and culture.

16.q: יִפְקֹ֣ד יְהוָ֔ה אֱלֹהֵ֥י הָ⁠רוּחֹ֖ת לְ⁠כָל בָּשָׂ֑ר אִ֖ישׁ עַל הָ⁠עֵדָֽה
16.note: The implication is that Moses is asking Yahweh to appoint a man to lead **the congregation**. You could include this information if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [May Yahweh, the God of the spirits of all flesh, appoint a man to lead the congregation]

Here, **all flesh** represents all living creatures. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [the God of the spirits of all living creatures]

17.q: אֲשֶׁר יֵצֵ֣א לִ⁠פְנֵי⁠הֶ֗ם וַ⁠אֲשֶׁ֤ר יָבֹא֙ לִ⁠פְנֵי⁠הֶ֔ם וַ⁠אֲשֶׁ֥ר יוֹצִיאֵ֖⁠ם וַ⁠אֲשֶׁ֣ר יְבִיאֵ֑⁠ם
17.note: Moses is referring to all of the activities of leading the people by naming two major components, **go out** and **come in**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [who will lead them in all their activities and who will direct them in everything they do]

Here, **their face** represents the presence of the people, that is, being in front of them. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before them]

17.q: וְ⁠לֹ֤א תִהְיֶה֙ עֲדַ֣ת יְהוָ֔ה כַּ⁠צֹּ֕אן אֲשֶׁ֥ר אֵין לָ⁠הֶ֖ם רֹעֶֽה
17.note: The point of this comparison is that just as **sheep** without a shepherd have no one to lead and protect them, so **the congregation of Yahweh** would have no one to lead and protect them if Yahweh did not appoint a leader. If it would be helpful in your language, you could make this point explicitly. Alternate translation: [and the congregation of Yahweh will not be left without anyone to lead and protect them]

Moses is using this possessive form to mean the congregation that belongs to Yahweh. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [the congregation that belongs to Yahweh]

18.note: Laying a hand on someone was a symbolic action by which Moses showed that he was giving Joshua authority to lead the people in his place. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could explain the significance of this action in the text of your translation or in a footnote. Alternate translation: [and you shall lay your hand on him to show that you are giving him your authority]

This could mean: (1) that Joshua has a **spirit** that is wise and capable. The phrase means that he is a wise and capable man, a good leader. Alternate translation: [in whom is skill and wisdom] (2) that Joshua has the Holy Spirit, which empowers him. Alternate translation: [in whom is my Spirit]

19.note: The pronoun **him** refers to Joshua, not to Eleazar. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [And you shall stand Joshua to the face of Eleazar the priest]

19.q: לִ⁠פְנֵי֙ אֶלְעָזָ֣ר הַ⁠כֹּהֵ֔ן וְ⁠לִ⁠פְנֵ֖י כָּל הָ⁠עֵדָ֑ה
19.note: Here, **the face of** represents the presence of a person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [before Eleazar the priest and before all the congregation]
See how you translated the similar expression in 27:14.

20.q: וְ⁠נָתַתָּ֥ה מֵ⁠הֽוֹדְ⁠ךָ֖ עָלָ֑י⁠ו לְמַ֣עַן יִשְׁמְע֔וּ כָּל עֲדַ֖ת בְּנֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל
20.note: Here, **so that** marks **all the congregation of the sons of Israel will hear** as the goal or purpose of **you shall give from your splendor on him**. Use a connector in your language that makes it clear that this is the purpose.

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **splendor**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [And you shall let him share in being majestic as you are]

Here, **your splendor** represents the authority that Yahweh had given to Moses. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [some of your authority]

21.note: See how you translated the similar expression in 27:19.

Here, the pronoun **he** could refer to: (1) Eleazar. In this case, Eleazar is asking Yahweh for the sake of Joshua. Alternate translation: [and Eleazar shall ask for Joshua] (2) Joshua. In this case, Joshua is asking Eleazar to ask Yahweh. Alternate translation: [and Joshua shall ask of Eleazar]

Here, the pronoun **his** in both places could refer to: (1) God. Alternate translation: [Yahweh’s mouth … his mouth] (2) Eleazar. Alternate translation: [Eleazar’s mouth … his mouth] (3) Joshua. Alternate translation: [Joshua’s mouth … his mouth]

If your language does not use an abstract noun for the idea of **the judgment**, you could express the same idea in another way. Alternate translation: [and he shall ask for him by using the Urim to learn what has been decided]

21.q: עַל פִּ֨י⁠ו יֵצְא֜וּ וְ⁠עַל פִּ֣י⁠ו יָבֹ֗אוּ
21.note: Here, **his mouth** represents what Eleazar would say after he learned the decision of Yahweh. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [According to what he says they shall go out and according to what he says they shall come in]

Yahweh is referring to all of the activities of the people by naming two major components, **go out** and **come in**. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [they shall conduct all of their affairs]

23.note: Here, **the hand of Moses** represents Moses himself as the one through whom Yahweh gave these commands. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [by means of Moses]
